finding.claim: Authorization result is discarded in dropTable, so any logged-in user can run DROP TABLE via /admin/drop (broken access control).
finding.source: Any authenticated caller with a user object in request context (api.go:25 userFrom) reaching the route registered at api.go:44.

trace.note: /admin/drop routed to dropTable with no auth wrapper in this file
userFrom loads the user from context
Authorize(u, "dba") called but its error is ignored, so execution continues for non-DBA users

finding.guards_checked: Authorize at api.go:13-20 correctly returns 'forbidden' when role is missing, but the return value is discarded at api.go:26. Sibling handler vacuum (api.go:33-36) checks and returns 403, so the missing check is specific to dropTable. No middleware in this file enforces role checks on the route.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check and it does return an error on a missing role, but its result is discarded by the bare call at api.go:26. No middleware in api.go wraps the route at api.go:44. The sibling vacuum handler (api.go:33-35) does check and return 403, so the omission is specific to dropTable.
verdict.reason: The call `Authorize(u, "dba")` at api.go:26 is a bare statement whose error is ignored, so `runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t"))` at api.go:27 runs for any user object in context reached via the route at api.go:44. The trace matches the file. The one thing this file cannot show is the authentication middleware that populates the "user" context value, so the "any logged-in user" premise rests on that being set upstream.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the 't' form value is concatenated unvalidated into a DROP TABLE statement.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27, fully attacker-controlled. Reachable by any user because of F1.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27 (runSQL stub at api.go:41).

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") concatenated into SQL string and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: No validation, identifier allowlist, quoting, or parameterization on t at api.go:27. The authz check at api.go:26 does not restrict the content of t and is ignored anyway.

verdict.guard_found: The only control is Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26, which returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. No parameterization, identifier allowlist, or quoting is applied to r.FormValue("t") before it is concatenated at api.go:27. The /admin/drop route is registered at api.go:44, and the trace matches the code.
verdict.reason: The attacker only needs a request that reaches dropTable with a user in context: api.go:26 calls Authorize without checking its error, so any authenticated user passes, and api.go:27 concatenates the attacker-controlled t directly into the SQL string. The caveat is that runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the injected SQL executing is assumed rather than shown in this code, and the user-in-context middleware is not in this file.
